title: Social Psychology
summary: The study of how individuals think, feel, and behave in social contexts — including conformity, obedience, group dynamics, social identity, and how situational pressures shape behavior.

content.title: Core Concept
content.content: Social psychology examines how social situations shape individual behavior. Key research traditions include Milgram's obedience studies, Asch's conformity experiments, Festinger's cognitive dissonance theory, Tajfel's social identity theory, and Cialdini's influence principles. A consistent finding: situational pressures are far more powerful predictors of behavior than personality traits.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Integrates This
content.content: TEG-Blue integrates social psychology across multiple frameworks. F4 maps how conformity and obedience function as nervous system regulation strategies. F5 uses social identity theory to explain how worth hierarchies produce in-group/out-group sorting. F6 draws on cognitive bias research to show how perception serves regulation rather than accuracy. F7 connects situational psychology to the escalation pathway from protection through domination.
